raw_response:
Let me think this through like I actually plan my year.

My land is 5 mu, and I run the cabbage-longbean-spinach rotation on the main 3 mu — spinach comes off in early spring, then longbean through summer, then cabbage goes in late summer for autumn harvest. The other 2 mu I keep separate: 1 mu chili (I transplant seedlings in April, pick through summer and autumn), and 1 mu maize for our own grain and to feed the chickens. Me and the wife, we can just manage this with some help at cabbage harvest.

Now for fertilizer, I been doing this 40 years so I know what these crops eat. Cabbage is the hungriest — heads won't pack tight without enough nitrogen. I use compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, maybe 50 kg per mu before transplant, then top-dress twice with urea. Total nitrogen around 22 kg. Cabbage worms and aphids are bad here, so I spray 5 times minimum. I use hybrid seed from the town shop, 北京新3号 type — all my neighbors use hybrid cabbage now, old types give loose heads.

Longbean doesn't need much nitrogen, the roots make their own. I give it a small base of compound fertilizer and one top-dress when flowering starts. Spinach is short season, quick grower — I just broadcast urea and some compound, irrigate from the well, done in 50 days.

Chili needs steady water and lots of K for fruit setting. This is where I spend more on spray — anthracnose and thrips will ruin a chili crop fast. I spray 7 times through the season.

Maize for ourselves — I don't push it. One base dressing, one top-dress at knee-high stage. Old habit, works fine.

I rotary till before cabbage and chili because they need loose soil. For maize I plough deeper every few years to break up the pan.
